title: Plugin Split Progress
eyebrow: Progress · the plugin split (#437): steps 1 to 3 built, draft pull request #452 open

short.lead: Steps 1, 2 and 3 of the plugin split are built, and I checked each result by running it myself. The draft pull request, #452, is open. It stays a draft until six checks pass. Half of the first is done: every suite passes here, but CI has not run yet.
short.hint: Tap a step for its evidence.
items: Plugins can depend on each other (#438)

Installing a test plugin printed "Successfully installed plugin: spike-a@spike-mkt (scope: user) (+ 1 dependency: spike-lib)". Two plugins that both block a reply run at the same time and both messages reach me. Every plugin sees the same stop_hook_active signal on the retry, so the lock has to count each check's blocks itself. Details are in the "Step 1 findings (#438)" section of docs/4-systems/plugin-split.md.

verify.py: 965 checks pass and exits 0. verify_tools.py: 50 checks pass. The drift check (every copy of the library matches its source) and the version-bump check (the plugin version was raised) pass. claude plugin install house-lib@aj-house-rules installed and enabled it from this repo in a throwaway config folder. House-rules is now 2.74.2.
Rule enforcement plugin (#440): part A built

Rule loading (the session-start rules, the rules sent to helpers, the per-message reminder) now lives in the new rule-enforcement plugin, and house-rules is 2.75.0. All four suites pass: house-rules 941 checks, rule-enforcement 35, tools 50, and the library drift check. In a real session with both plugins installed, each rule section loaded exactly once. I fixed two pointers that led from one plugin into the other (commit 7521340). The notes that house-rules used to add inside the rules text now arrive as their own messages, worded the same.
The repeat-failure lock (#440): part B built

A check that keeps failing blocks the reply three times, then source edits and commits are refused until it passes. The action that fixes the failing check is always allowed: when the commit check is locked, commits still go through. Checked: house-rules 952 checks pass, rule-enforcement 60 pass, the library copies match. In the recorded live session, a missing commit blocked three times, then a source edit was refused, the commit went through, and the lock cleared.
Three ways around the lock, closed

The shell command sed -i (an in-place edit) on the locked file is now refused, and the file stays unchanged. A reply that wrote nothing no longer clears the lock. A command run from another folder now meets the lock too. Committing the locked file still clears the lock, as intended. Checked: house-rules 959 checks pass, rule-enforcement 94 pass.
Part C of step 3: the off switches, removed

I removed 19 off switches, and the off setting of the permission timer. The checks they controlled now always run. The helper-record switch is kept, as you asked. Checked: house-rules 936 checks pass, rule-enforcement 95, tools 55. In a live session, setting HOUSE_RULES_LOOP=off changed nothing. While I worked, main gained a reference page for plans and pitches. I merged main into this branch, and every suite still passes.
Two rule paths that pointed at the wrong plugin

House-rules now names the real paths of the page builder (make_page.py) and the handover output style at the start of every session. A live session printed the page builder's path, and running that file worked. A new test fails if the rules ever name a file their plugin does not hold.
Draft pull request #452 and its six checks

Done: every suite passes locally (house-rules 937 checks, rule-enforcement 96, tools 55, the library copy check and the version-bump check). Still to run: (1) the same suites in CI on the pull request. (2) A replay of every hook through main's 2.74.1 and through this branch, with every difference traced to something you approved. (3) Real sessions showing no tool is refused that 2.74.1 allows. (4) A clean install from GitHub. (5) A tested one-step rollback. (6) Your QA pass.
Say whether I should watch #452 for CI results and review comments.
